chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: Martin's on the Plaza: the restaurant and its schedule
summary: The Plaza was an elite area; the band played soft music then dance music, 20 minutes on and 40 off.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Uh-huh. But somehow, Mr. Bayles (in and Martin audible) that owned that place --
Yeah. Mr. Bayles might have had some interest in it.
(Bayliss) was a real estate man, wasn't he?
Yeah. And they were good friends. You see, this was a real ritzy part of Kansas City at that time. The Plaza, you know. All those beautiful homes, and trees in the yards, gardens and things.
But you say it was Martin's on the Plaza?
Well, what was the Plaza? Was it a
Yeah. It was -- that part of Kansas City was known as the Plaza.
Well, I mean, was it like a plaza and in Europe you have a big square with houses around it?

It wasn't exactly a square, but it was like an area that was -- the whole area was well kept, with the fine homes. And it did have some shops and things like that. It was like for the elite society, you know.

This was a restaurant, and they had a little anteroom there that was a club. But what we played was in the restaurant part. And the first part of the night, I think up until 10:00 o'clock, from eight until 10:00, we played just soft music, and the guys singing. Then the waiters would come out and move all the chairs and tables and everything, then we played dance music.
But they had us playing 20 and 40. Play 20 and had 40 minutes off. And that was so people would spend money drinking that time.
